newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end firm, but profit-taking seen.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end firm, but profit-taking seen.

text.p: Caracas stocks surged for the third straight day on strong foreign bids, but traders and analysts said the rally was overblown and profit-taking was likely in coming sessions.

"I think the market's overreacting. Nothing fundamental has changed, either in the economy or corporate results ... The bolsa's been pulled up by stocks with ADR listings," said Merinvest analyst Roberto Isasi.
The bourse's 19-share index closed up 1.25 percent at 6,531.48 points with analysts seeing resistance at 6,600.

"There seems to be rising interest in the country ... both equities and international debt are up," said Interacciones broker Piero Montelli, who added, however, that stocks were increasingly looking overvalued.
Traders said foreign interest has been piqued by apparent progress in the privatization program and a slew of favorable comments recently from the IMF.

Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said Tuesday the government and the IMF both saw growth of up to four percent this year, rising to five percent next year, with inflation falling to 14 percent in 1998.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, trade volume reached a high of 62 million shares, worth 7.2 billion bolivars ($15 million), as 23 stocks rose, 13 fell and five closed flat.
Telephone company CANTV led gainers closing up 40 bolivars at 2270.00. Merinvest's composite index, which includes CANTV, rose 1.36 percent to end at 103.11.

Among the day's other main traders, brokers singled out gains in blue chips such as foods company Mavesa, up 0.75 bolivar to finish at 91.75, Electricidad de Caracas, up 9.00 bolivars to close at 547.00, and textiles company Mantex, up 0.15 percent in heavy trade to end at 39.40.
